minutes.headline: Personnel Committee scored seven job descriptions for grading and heard the DPW director say the scoring weights are wrong.
minutes.summary: The committee spent most of the meeting rating job descriptions category by category: facilities director, land use director, network administrator, payroll/benefits coordinator and risk manager, principal assessor, and treasurer/tax collector. Two descriptions (executive assistant, park manager) were deferred because none is approved. After the job reviews, the committee heard a report on vacation accrual practice across groups and concluded no change was needed.

public_comment.topic: The DPW director said the scoring weights over-weight hazards, work environment and physical demands compared with knowledge and experience, compared them with a federal system, and urged the committee to re-examine its weighting.
Closing public comment was invited; no comment is captured.

votes.motion: Move ongoing business on vacation leave accrual to after new business

decisions.decision: Executive assistant to the town manager and select board deferred until a job description is approved.
Park manager review deferred to a future meeting because no job description is available.
Facilities director left about 150 points off the target grade; committee agreed to move on and return to it.
Principal assessor total looked low against its current grade; flagged for revisiting.
Treasurer/tax collector flagged as an outlier; the committee will revisit it along with the park manager and executive assistant.
No change to the vacation accrual practice; the committee found no disparity between groups.

what_happened.line: The committee scored seven job descriptions category by category, leaving the facilities director well off its target grade and flagging the principal assessor as low.
The DPW director told the committee its scoring weights over-weight hazards, work environment and physical demands relative to knowledge and experience.
The treasurer/tax collector scored as an outlier and will be revisited with the park manager and executive assistant.
The executive assistant and park manager reviews were deferred because no job description is approved or available.
The committee found no disparity in vacation accrual between groups and made no change to the practice.

why_it_matters: The scores set how town jobs are graded, and grades drive pay, so the weighting questions raised here could shift what the town pays for several positions that show up in future budgets.
Vacation accrual stays as it is, so no leave-cost change follows from this meeting.
